assessment.nobel_worthiness: Obstfeld and Rogoff turned open-economy macroeconomics into an intertemporal, microfounded field with the Redux model, and their textbook set the standard framework. They also named the exchange-rate disconnect and related puzzles that still structure the research agenda. The framework underpins how central banks and the IMF analyse current accounts, exchange rates and spillovers.
assessment.attribution: The two are the clear joint originators of the intertemporal approach to the current account and of the New Open Economy Macroeconomics synthesis. Other contributors exist, such as Svensson, Sachs, Corsetti and Gopinath, but the core credit is concentrated in these two. The credited list also includes work by Rogoff on exchange-rate puzzles that is separable from the joint program.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s and has had decades of use, replication and extension. International macroeconomics has not been recognised recently, so timing is favourable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the contribution as a distinct discovery or as an extension of the Mundell-Fleming tradition.
Rogoff appears on another ballot (B011), which could split support.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Melitz (2003) is among the most influential papers in modern trade. It integrated firm heterogeneity and selection into general-equilibrium trade models, which changed how gains from trade, exporter premia and reallocation are understood. Firm-level microdata and heterogeneous-firm models are now standard well beyond trade, including in the macro and growth work on firm dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator. Helpman is the natural co-recipient through his role in the new trade theory, the heterogeneous-firm exporting and FDI literature, and the empirical firm-level work. Redding is a strong contributor to the quantitative follow-ups but is later. Bernard, Eaton, Kortum and Jensen are important and are not credited here, so there is a real attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across theory, structural estimation and microdata. The Krugman prize in 2008 covered the earlier new trade theory but not the firm-heterogeneity wave.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would want to include Bernard, Eaton and Kortum.
Helpman appears on two ballots (B001 and B030), so support may split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour-market adjustment, polarization and the distributional costs of trade and automation. The work combines credible empirical design with a conceptual framework and has had very large policy and academic impact.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to the task and polarization strand. The China shock strand is Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task model also owes much to Acemoglu, who is already a laureate, and to Zeira and Restrepo, who are not credited here. Katz is credited on the ballot but would be a fourth, which exceeds the limit.
assessment.maturity: The task literature has been developing since 2003, and the China shock papers have been replicated and debated since 2013. Recent debate on the persistence and magnitude of effects is itself evidence of maturity, though the work is still evolving.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and with Acemoglu's task-model work.
Ongoing debate over the size and persistence of the trade-shock effects and the research design.
Choosing three from four credited names is a judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors created the modern long-run top-income and wealth-distribution evidence base from tax and national accounts data, and they developed methods for estimating offshore wealth. This reoriented the field and public debate about inequality. The empirical and data-construction contribution is large, and it fed into the World Inequality Database.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the clear originators of the top-incomes series. Zucman is a major later contributor on wealth and offshore evidence. Atkinson is deceased and cannot be credited.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from the early 2000s and has been extended to many countries. The wealth-distribution and offshore estimates are newer and still contested.
uncertainties: Methodological dispute about distributional national accounts and wealth estimates.
Whether the committee treats the contribution as measurement or as economic theory.
Saez is also credited on B045, which could split support.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian synthesis and the rule-based theory of monetary policy are the core of modern central-bank practice. Calvo contributed the pricing mechanism, Taylor the staggered contracts and the policy rule, and Woodford the micro-founded policy framework. The practical and academic impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across eight listed names, including Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, and also others not listed, such as Rotemberg, Clarida and Fischer. Any three-person selection leaves out serious contributors, which is a real weakness. I chose the three who most clearly originated the pricing, rule and framework components.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested for 30 or more years in theory and in practice. The 2008 crisis and the 2021-23 inflation episode both raised questions about the framework.
uncertainties: Dispersed attribution is the main risk to a clean three-person award.
The 2022 prize recognised related banking and monetary work, which may reduce appetite.
The framework has been challenged by the inflation episode and by heterogeneous-agent models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation literature quantified how the distribution of productivity and distortions across firms explains much of the cross-country income gap, linking micro data to macro development accounting. It reshaped development and growth research and has been applied widely to policy questions. I note a conflict: Klenow is a long-running co-author of mine, which is disclosed and not adjudicated here. I tried to apply the same criteria as for other candidates and ranked it below several others for that reason.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) and Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) are the two founding papers, so Rogerson is a conspicuous omission from the credited list. Banerjee and Duflo and Jovanovic also contributed to the idea, which makes attribution contested.
assessment.maturity: More than 15 years of replication and extension, with extensive debate on measurement error and on the interpretation of dispersion. The 2025 prize recognised growth through innovation, so the area has been honoured recently.
uncertainties: The omission of Rogerson from the credited names weakens the attribution.
Debate about whether measured dispersion reflects distortions or measurement error.
Recent recognition of growth theory in 2025 may reduce near-term appetite.
My conflict with Klenow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley developed formal political economics covering electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal outcomes and state capacity, and tested the predictions empirically. This created a core field and a standard textbook. The work links institutions to policy outcomes in a way that is conceptually distinct from the institutions-and-prosperity prize of 2024.
assessment.attribution: Attribution to these three is natural and coherent, since they developed the field jointly and individually through the comparative-politics program. Persson is a former committee member, so I treat this as a possible institutional-conflict point for the group, not a merit issue. Alesina and Drazen are significant contributors who are not credited, and Alesina is deceased.
assessment.maturity: Work from the 1990s and 2000s, extensively built upon. Adjacent institutions research was honoured in 2024, so timing is slightly less favourable.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2024 prize on institutions.
Whether the committee sees the contribution as a unified discovery or a field-building effort.
Persson's past committee role could be treated as a conflict by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints create a dynamic amplification and propagation mechanism that links credit conditions to asset prices and output. This is central to how macroeconomists model financial frictions and crises. The mechanism informed both academic work and policy thinking after 2008.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint credit cycle. Bernanke-Gertler and the financial accelerator literature is related but partly recognised already, since Bernanke received the 2022 prize. I left out Gertler and Gilchrist to keep the credit specific to the collateral mechanism, though this is a judgement.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of use as a workhorse mechanism, with a large literature after the financial crisis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Whether the committee prefers to include Gertler and Gilchrist for the financial accelerator.
The contribution is a single seminal paper plus follow-ups, which may weigh against breadth.
